source.title: The Local Learning Coefficient: A Singularity-Aware Complexity Measure
source.authors: Edmund Lau; Zach Furman; George Wang; Daniel Murfet; Susan Wei

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test accuracy and training loss alongside LLC across optimizer settings, and reports how those quantities vary. This is a different measure and an indirect test of the optimizer-related gap claim; it does not test the claim’s generalization gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ResNet18 test accuracy and training loss under learning-rate, batch-size, momentum, and explicit L2-regularization sweeps, but does not report numerical train-test error gaps. LLC is a complexity measurement, not itself a generalization-gap measure. The paper’s cited claims about memorization and prior sharpness/generalization studies are not its own results.
record.test_reason: The study tests LLC estimation and reports related generalization results, but none tests a listed version. Its batch-size sweeps hold optimizer iterations fixed, so epoch budgets vary with batch size; they do not test V5's fixed-epoch comparison. LLC is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Neither missing train-test gaps nor the absence of adaptive optimizers alone explains all exclusions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's empirical paraphrase is accurate: higher learning rate, smaller batches and higher momentum accompany lower LLC and higher test accuracy; stronger L2 regularization accompanies lower LLC. The authors also validate estimator accuracy and scalability using deep linear networks. They do not establish that LLC predicts generalization generally; Appendix E explicitly leaves its connection to generalization beyond Bayesian learning unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates local learning coefficients using SGLD and reports test accuracy in optimizer and regularization sweeps; the claim versions concern memorization and generalization gaps, which the paper does not directly test.
record.method_sensitivity: In ResNet18 on CIFAR10, reported LLC and test-accuracy curves vary with learning rate, batch size, and momentum. The paper also reports lower LLC with stronger L2 regularization. These are separate single-factor sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher learning rates and momentum accompany lower LLC and higher test accuracy in the ResNet18 CIFAR10 sweeps; training loss reaches zero in most settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these single-factor SGD sweeps, learning rate and momentum influence estimated LLC and held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches accompany lower LLC and higher test accuracy when training runs use the same number of optimizer iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For ResNet18 on CIFAR10 at learning rate 0.01 and 100000 updates, smaller batches improve held-out accuracy, both with and without momentum.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger L2 regularization accompanies lower estimated LLC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit L2 regularization can reduce estimated LLC in the reported ResNet18 CIFAR10 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropy-SGD yields lower LLC than SGD on MNIST; both estimates are approximately 1000 for a network with 1863690 parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entropy-SGD finds minima with lower estimated LLC than SGD in this MNIST experiment.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The ResNet LLC estimates cannot be calibrated against true LLC values. The authors manually remove rare negative estimates or divergent SGLD chains. The LLC estimator depends on SGLD hyperparameters, which are calibrated per experiment set rather than each run. Several plotted outcomes have no exact numerical values in the text. The study does not directly report train-test error gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows were left out under the row limit. Deep linear network results validate LLC estimation against theoretical learning coefficients but do not report a result on the claim’s generalization behavior. Language-model LLC estimates similarly do not test a claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects with epochs held fixed, and whether recipe adaptations remove those effects.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and joint dropout-and-weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus train-test error gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T2 classification is inconsistent with its correctly unlinked rows. The batch-size findings concern held-out accuracy directly, so numerical train-test gaps are unnecessary for that comparison; the decisive mismatch with V5 is the varying epoch budget. States marked cannot_determine concern the listed versions, not whether the paper reports its separate LLC associations.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels versus generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and subsequent test-accuracy changes.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss generalization and sharpness, but the study's own results address LLC estimation and its response to training heuristics rather than a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: No listed version is tested or used as a tool. Batch-size sweeps fix iterations rather than epochs; LLC is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness; the remaining sweeps do not measure the comparisons required by the other versions.

source_check.notes: Exact plotted outcomes are figure-only; the qualitative associations are stated explicitly. Appendix E leaves the connection between learning coefficients and generalization beyond the Bayesian setting unresolved.
